headline: Scientists have kept silicon quantum bits above 99.99% accuracy while running three of them at the same time, by fixing a control problem that normally degrades them.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed, clear technical advance for silicon qubits, but on a five-qubit lab device.
importance_line: Being able to drive many silicon qubits at once through one shared control line is a step toward large chips that can be made in ordinary semiconductor factories, but the demonstration is five qubits and quantum computers will need millions.
summary: Researchers report in Nature Physics that in a five-qubit silicon spin device they traced the drop in accuracy during parallel operation to microwave-driven energy shifts (a.c.-Stark shifts) and removed it with a simple calibration of qubit pairs, giving gate fidelities well above 99.99% for single qubits and above 99.99% with three running together. With all five qubits running at once fidelity stayed above 99.9%, the level widely targeted for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
notes: Phys.org blocked (403); read the Nature Physics paper itself (Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array). Author team and institutions not captured in the text read, so none are named.
